meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now show me what you're basing it on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He told me he wrote it over the weekend, and a paste from another file looks exactly like that. Did you ask him that before you entered the zero?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Is anything on his record right now, and who else has seen that screen?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
A wrong line is a seventeen-year-old misquoting from memory or citing the wrong scene. Have you searched the whole play, or only that one? And you skipped my question: his record.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
I'll check that against the play myself. Twice now you've gone past his record, so hear it plainly: whatever happens, nothing goes on it and this stays quiet. What is it you want from him?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
An outline is two weeks before the essay, and students change their argument; that's what an outline is for. You keep turning screens and not answering me, Hale. What are you asking for?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4. He'll do it, to put this behind him and not because he did anything wrong. In writing tonight, with the date of the rewrite and the words nothing on his record.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth. He'll be there. Put the time and the room in tonight's email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Cc: Principal

Hale,

You agreed under procedure 4.4 to a private supervised rewrite for Owen on Thursday the twelfth after school, not in front of his class, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require the time and the room for Thursday, and your answers to the two questions you went past: whether Owen was spoken to before the zero was entered, and who else has seen this material. I expect all of it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record. She still wants that in writing tonight with the time and room, plus answers on whether Owen was spoken to first and who else has seen the evidence. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it well before her time ran out.
What moved her: you showed the version history with its exact times and, when she said he had pasted it in from another file, you asked for that dated draft. It was a dated document she could check herself, and her one defence had nowhere to go.
What cost ground: you went past her question about his record twice and showed another document instead. His record is the thing she fears most, so each dodge made her sharper and left her with open points for the email.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history put the essay's creation at 11:31 PM on Wednesday, October 28, with the text arriving at 11:52 PM and 11:58 PM, which is a late night in October and as close as anything said came to that night. It proves nothing about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she asked whether anything was on his record and who else had seen your screen, answer both in one sentence before you show the quotation, so the thing she fears most is settled while your evidence is still landing.
